Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on batching/caching for AscendAI pilot

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team liked the latency numbers but we need to understand trade-offs for our peak workloads before we sign the pilot SOW. Two quick asks:

- Do you have recommended batching/window sizes for short multi-turn chat (avg turn ~15 tokens, peak concurrency ~220)?
- How does Redwood's prefix/KV caching interact with our session routing — will cache warmups cause token spikes that affect costs?
- We're considering an 8-bit quantized profile to save GPU memory; any known quality regressions for instruction-following models?

I attached a small sample of our production metrics (ascend_prod_metrics.csv). Would love to set a 30-min tech sync next week so your engineers can recommend a config.

Cheers,
Tom
Director of ML Platforms
AscendAI

Attached: ascend_prod_metrics.csv

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Questions on batching/caching for AscendAI pilot

Internal planning note — draft playbook for the 30-min tech sync with AscendAI (Tom/Sana). Please review and flag anything I miss.

Goal: deliver a recommended initial config that keeps 95th-latency <= 220ms for single-shot and decent tail behavior for multi-turn while minimizing token cost during warmups.

Key recommendations (starter values):
- Batching: target dynamic batch cap = 32 tokens / 8 requests per batch for multi-turn chat (avg turn 15 tokens). Start conservative: max_batch_size = 32, batch_time_ms = 12. Rationale: limits per-request queuing while amortizing kernel overhead.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching with per-session TTL = 1800s for active conversational sessions. Add a warmed-request threshold (e.g., 3 requests) before counting session as cached in metrics. Mitigation: implement short cache-priming policy (send 1 warmup request from client during session start) to avoid large on-demand warmup spikes.
- Quantization: recommend 8-bit (PTQ) for initial staging only; run rolling quality checks against our eval set — if instruction-following BLEU/ROUGE delta > 1.5 points, fallback to 16-bit or mixed quant profile. Note known regressions are model-dependent; Rishi to provide model-specific guidance.
- Routing: configure routing policy to prefer cheaper region/variant for background/low-priority inference. Implement hard latency SLO fallback to the higher-performance model pool for requests tagged "interactive".

Owner/next actions:
- Rishi: prepare short runbook for model-specific quantization checks and a script to run evals on their sample metrics (due Tue COB).
- Monica: coordinate time with Tom/Sana and confirm traffic split (multi-turn % vs single-shot) before the call. Also prepare a shared doc to capture action items.
- Jasmine: capture the session notes and send back the recommended config and SOW note for pilot acceptance.

Attachments: planning matrix below attached (ASC_implementation_matrix.xlsx). I'll bring the matrix to the call so we can mark decisions live.

Thanks — please add any quick wins I missed (e.g., token truncation policies, early-stop defaults).

Jasmine Liu
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attached: ASC_implementation_matrix.xlsx

Jasmine — this looks great, thanks for the clear playbook. A few quick datapoints ahead of Wed's call:

- Multi-turn %: ~42% of requests are multi-turn (mostly short follow-ups).
- Early-stop: happens ~8% of the time (clients send stop tokens or we apply top-p cutoff).
- Peak concurrency: we can hit 220 at peak; baseline weekday peaks are ~120.
- We're happy to start with the conservative batch settings you proposed and validate on a small canary (10% traffic).

I'll upload an expanded metric extract to the Drive folder you shared and confirm an attendee list from our infra team. Wed 11:00 PT works for us.
